newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $1-dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $1-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Wednesday were seen steady to $1.00 per cwt higher, lifted by ongoing light hog movement, livestock dealers said.
The light hog marketings had packers competing and paying higher for live inventory despite reduced operations brought on by unprofitable margins since late April, they said.
Even with the suspension this week of second shift operations at John Morrell and Co's Sioux Falls, S.D., hog plant, demand still exceeded suppies, the dealers said.
"They're just not out there, there's not enough hogs," said one central Iowa hog buyer.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to the plant could range $57.50 to $58.00. Illinois top prices for hogs at the plant were seen at $56.50 to $57.00 as were Indiana/Ohio top prices.
Light support also was expected from outlooks for higher trending pork prices, the dealers said.
Some of that strength, however, could be diluted by sentiment that the gains were based on lower supply instead of active retail or export demand, the dealers said.
Lighter hog marketings were seen translating into smaller pork production, they said.
